claims.notes: [BATCH NOTE b083 RE-EXTRACT 2] Second wholesale replacement of 083 in the same day, under charter § 5 rule 14 (ruling 18): the source document received a SECOND revision on 2026-08-04 and grew from 189 to 211 lines. Three things moved — (a) the § 1 ground-truth feature count now carries two figures in one span, (b) the § 4 F1 rank figure for the image run moved from 0.8332 to 0.8333, and (c) a 'Second revision, same day' block was appended inside the 2026-08-04 Changelog entry (lines 179-199) carrying its own before/after table and an explicitly open adjudication question. Line anchors at and below line 179 shifted by +22; lines 1-178 are unchanged in numbering. LIVE-VERSUS-HISTORICAL SPLIT, CHANGELOG TABLE 1 (lines 151-157, the Methods reconciliation): each row is one claim (rule 6); the Before cell is `historical` with path null, the After cell is the live `read` claim. On the Methodology-mirror row (line 155) TWO of three values are historical — the Before cell AND the mirror's own 1,000/percentile settings that the After cell explicitly preserves as historical fact; only `--bootstrap 10000` is live. LIVE-VERSUS-HISTORICAL SPLIT, CHANGELOG TABLE 2 (lines 181-184, the second revision): same rule. Line 183 splits 4,744 (Before, `historical`, path null) from 4,746 (After, live `read` at `len:$.features` in the GT GeoJSON); line 184 splits 0.8332 (Before, `historical`) from 0.8333 (After, live `read` at $.results[0].F1 in the image corrected-F1 summary). The prose under the table (lines 186-190) restates both pairs and is split the same way. § 1 DUAL-FIGURE SPAN (line 20): the single Ground-truth bullet now asserts a live figure and a historical one side by side, so the two values take DIFFERENT methods inside one claim per v1.2 amendment 3 — 4,746 is `read` with its own explicit path `len:$.features`, 4,744 is `historical` with path null, and the count of curator additions ('two') is `anchor-unknown` because it is decidable only from the GT GeoJSON's git history. No value in that span is left pathless-and-read. THE 4,745 REFERENCES — BIGGEST JUDGEMENT CALL OF THIS PASS, FLAGGED FOR TRIAGE: the document's new text (lines 192-195) states that the '4,745-mound updated curator ground truth' references in the header, § 2, § 7 and the original-publication stub are 'deliberately left as historical narrative ... not the current artefact'. The live GT GeoJSON now holds 4,746 features, so the previous extraction's treatment of those spans as live `read` claims against `len:$.features` would now fabricate four mismatches. They are therefore RECLASSIFIED to `historical` at lines 11, 40, 104 and 211 (and in the new block's own quotation at lines 192-195). The ONE exception is § 2 line 31 ('All four are evaluated over ... the canonical 4,745-mound updated curator GT'), which the document itself escalates as an open adjudication question rather than resolving: that value is classed `anchor-unknown`, deliberately neither `historical` (which would assert it superseded) nor `read` (which would assert it current). Triage owns the era question; the chase targets are the evaluation artefacts' `_metadata.generated_at_utc` timestamps against the 2026-05-03 curator-addition commits `baf1497a7` and `2e075eb99`. SCOPE DECISIONS (unchanged from the previous pass): dates, timestamps, git commit hashes (`163161a4`, `42ed1d32`, `580f498b6`, `0699769c5`, `bdd61bcc`, `98b128ae`, `7b7509d5`, `da2cf355f`, `fc536a19c`, `e86bca52d`, `baf1497a7`, `2e075eb99`), session numbers (Session 105), Obs identifiers (Obs 252/272/280/284), wave, pass and erratum identifiers (wave-7, P4, W6-E9), charter rule and ruling numbers (§ 5 rule 14, ruling 18), section cross-references (§ 1, § 2, § 3, § 4, § 7), the working-notes line citations (L13642, L11047), candidate identifiers (cand 2397, cand 4264), version strings (v2), Track 1 / Track 2 labels, and numbers inside file paths or condition names (`384/`, `55maps-...`, `T=0.3`, `T=0.7`, `t0.3`) are all out of C4 scope per instrument rule 5. '55-map' asserted as a corpus size IS extracted (rule 5's '487-tile Era 2 corpus' precedent). Buffer radii are extracted where the document asserts them as a grid, a cap, or a table cell (rule 6); radii appearing inline purely to label which row a quoted metric belongs to ('F1 @50m', 'at R = 50 m', 'the 50 m corrected F1') are treated as context. MCC TRAP (ruling 3): this document quotes STORED POINT estimates, so every MCC / sensitivity / specificity value is anchored at `.point`, never `.mean`; the two differ in these artefacts (e.g. image MCC point 0.6924 vs mean 0.6925) and must not be reconciled with a tolerance. ANCHOR PREFERENCE: § 2 and § 3 MCC figures are anchored to the LIVE `outputs/<run>/full-buffer-eval/evaluation.json` in preference to the archived per-run `mcc/evaluation.json` the document cites in § 7; the sole exception is 55maps-text-high-t0.3-generalisation, which has NO full-buffer-eval directory, so its MCC cells are anchored to `archive/55maps-superseded-gt-evals/per-run/55maps-text-high-t0.3-generalisation/mcc/evaluation.json`. Bootstrap parameters (10,000 / seed 42 / BCa) anchor to the artefacts' `_metadata.bootstrap` block. Map-count claims anchor to `$.inputs.n_maps` in the sibling buffer-100m diagnostic, the only JSON artefact in scope recording the corpus size.
